subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The median of 3, 7, 8, 12, 15, 20 is
questions.explain: With six values the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th, (8+12)/2 = 10.

questions.q: Using a regression line to predict outside the range of the data is called
questions.explain: Predicting beyond the observed data range is extrapolation, which is unreliable.

questions.q: A data set has mean 50 and standard deviation 6. Using mean plus or minus 2 standard deviations as outlier limits, the upper limit is
Why is the median often preferred over the mean for skewed data?
options: It is less affected by extreme values
questions.explain: The median is resistant to outliers and skew, unlike the mean which they pull.

questions.q: A PMCC of r = -0.92 indicates
questions.explain: A value near -1 indicates strong negative linear correlation.

questions.q: A box plot displays all of the following EXCEPT
questions.explain: A box plot shows the minimum, quartiles, median and maximum, but not the mean.

questions.q: For data with total 250 over 10 readings, the mean is
questions.explain: The mean is the total divided by the count, 250/10 = 25.

questions.q: A frequency table lists values 1, 2, 3 with frequencies 4, 6, 10. The mean is
The mode is the most appropriate average for
questions.explain: The mode is the only average usable for non-numeric categorical data, as it is the most frequent category.

questions.q: Standard deviation is measured in
options: the same units as the data
questions.explain: Standard deviation, being the square root of the variance, shares the same units as the original data.

questions.q: The 60th percentile of a distribution is the value below which
questions.explain: The 60th percentile is the value below which 60 percent of the ordered data fall.

questions.q: The mean of 4, 8, 9, 10 and 14 is
questions.explain: The sum is 45 and 45 divided by 5 equals 9.

questions.q: A grouped table has class 10-20 (width 10) with frequency 30. On a histogram its bar height (frequency density) is
questions.explain: Frequency density = 30/10 = 3.

questions.q: If y = (x - 100)/5 and the mean of y is 4, the mean of x is
If y = x/4 and the standard deviation of x is 12, the standard deviation of y is
questions.explain: Dividing each value by 4 divides the standard deviation by 4, so 12/4 = 3.

questions.q: A correlation between ice-cream sales and drownings does not prove ice cream causes drownings because
questions.explain: A strong correlation may reflect a lurking variable such as hot weather; correlation does not establish causation.

questions.q: A class of width 5 has frequency 20. Its frequency density is
questions.explain: Frequency density = frequency divided by class width, 20/5 = 4.

questions.q: A PMCC of r = 0.05 suggests
options: very little or no linear correlation
questions.explain: An r close to zero indicates almost no linear relationship between the variables.

questions.q: The interquartile range is
questions.explain: The IQR is the upper quartile minus the lower quartile, Q3 - Q1.

questions.q: For data with sum x = 50, sum x^2 = 300 and n = 10, the variance is
For the values 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 the mean is 14 and the population variance is
questions.explain: Squared deviations 16+4+0+4+16 = 40; 40/5 = 8.

questions.q: The variance of a data set is 16. Its standard deviation is
questions.explain: Standard deviation is the square root of the variance, and the square root of 16 is 4.

questions.q: Using the 1.5 times IQR rule, with Q1 = 20 and Q3 = 40, an upper outlier is any value above
With Q1 = 12 and Q3 = 28, the lower outlier boundary using 1.5 times IQR is
If each data value is coded as y = x - 10, the standard deviation of y compared with that of x is
questions.explain: Adding or subtracting a constant shifts the data but does not change the spread, so the standard deviation is unchanged.

questions.q: The median lies in the class 20 to 30 (width 10). The cumulative frequency below 20 is 8, the class frequency is 12, and the median position is the 14th of 28 values. By linear interpolation the median is
On a cumulative frequency graph, the median is read at a cumulative frequency of
questions.explain: The median corresponds to the n/2 point on the cumulative frequency axis.

questions.q: A class of width 8 has frequency density 2.5. Its frequency is
questions.explain: Frequency = frequency density times class width, 2.5 times 8 = 20.

questions.q: Predicting a value within the range of the observed data is called
questions.explain: Estimating within the data range is interpolation and is generally more reliable.

questions.q: The mode of 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 7, 7, 9 is
questions.explain: The value 7 occurs most often, three times.
